items.label: Focuslight Technologies half-year report: 2026 Half-Year Report (08-08-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Automotive (half-year report): in April 2026 customer 'AG company'

set.signal: Automotive (half-year report): an overseas projection-lighting customer placed no new pull orders after adjusting its purchasing strategy and the two sides not agreeing on subsequent commercial terms; headlamp MLA business was stable in H1, but with some projects late in their lifecycle and some customers delaying or slowing deliveries, H2 demand is expected to decline, affecting full-year revenue. As of the report date all previously disclosed lidar design-win projects with customer 'AG company' (a European automotive Tier1, as the company names it) are cancelled and no new lidar business is expected near term; lidar revenue was about 0.29% of total revenue as of June 30, 2026. The company is shifting more resources to optical communications and consumer electronics.

items.reason: Depth rule: the April 2026 / April 2025 cancellation details (about 50 and 15 ten-thousand sets) are already on the node under the 2025 Annual Report (04-29-2026) label; keep only what the half-year report adds (0.29%, projection-lighting customer, headlamp MLA H2 outlook, resource shift).

items.label: Infineon press release: Infineon enters into agreement to sell NOR Flash and F-RAM (09-16-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Infineon entered into a definitive agreement under which Winbond Electronics will acquire

set.signal: Infineon entered into a definitive agreement under which Winbond Electronics will acquire Infineon's NOR Flash and F-RAM business (NOR Flash memory and F-RAM products serving automotive, industrial and infrastructure customers); subject to regulatory approvals, the parties currently target closing in the second half of 2027. Winbond will operate the business as a standalone entity headquartered in Silicon Valley. Infineon retains its specialty memory portfolio (SRAM, HYPERRAM, nvSRAM and SONOS-based radiation-hardened memory). Peter Schiefer, President of the Automotive Division: the sale 'allows Infineon to further focus its portfolio and capital allocation on its core growth drivers'.

items.reason: Deal consideration form ('all-cash transaction') is a deal term, like the price the enricher already dropped (SKILL §2: operating facts of an acquisition only); everything else matches the release.
items.evidence: will acquire Infineon's NOR Flash and F-RAM business in an all-cash transaction valued at $1.12 billion on a cash and debt free basis
